# EvScrollArea

> The scroll component is the thin scrollbar indicator shown alongside an overflowing container, signalling that more content is available and how far the user has scrolled.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| ID | `evoq-ui:scroll-area` |
| Layer | Atom (`src/atoms`) |
| Import | `import { EvScrollArea } from 'evoq-ui'` |
| Template tag | `<EvScrollArea>` or `<ev-scroll-area>` |
| Source | `src/atoms/scroll-area/EvScrollArea.vue` |
| Extra attributes go to | the root `<div class="ev-scroll-area">` |

## Example

```vue
<EvScrollArea>
  <p v-for="n in 12" :key="n">Baris {{ n }}</p>
</EvScrollArea>
```

## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Scrollbar**, frame `4432:84149` (Scroll). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Shown automatically on a scrollable container to indicate overflow and scroll position. Use Vertical for tall content, Horizontal for wide content like tables or carousels.

### When not to use

- Don't add a scrollbar to content that fits without overflow. Don't use it as a draggable progress or range control — use a Slider (`evoq-ui:slider`) for that.

### Do

- Keep the bar subtle and let it fade when idle. Size the thumb to reflect the proportion of visible content. Use Mirror for right-to-left layouts or left-edge scrollbars.

### Don't

- Don't make the bar so thin it's hard to grab, or so prominent it competes with content. Don't hide it entirely where users rely on it to gauge length.

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvScrollArea`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the root `<div class="ev-scroll-area">`.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:scroll-area` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
